newsitem.title: UK: Suez Canal offers discount on Iraq oil - report.
newsitem.headline: Suez Canal offers discount on Iraq oil - report.

text.p: The Suez Canal authority has offered a discount on Iraqi crude oil shipments using the waterway, the London-based Saudi newspaper al-Hayat reported, OPEC news agency said on Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted the chairman of the authority, Ahmed Fadel, saying the authority had adopted a new policy of discount on any shipments that economic studies proved feasible.
The resumption of Iraqi exports through a Turkish pipeline under a food-for-oil exchange arranged by the United Nations could reduce demand for oil shipments through the Canal, he noted.
"We are trying to minimize that effect," he said.
Details of the discount were not given.
Most Iraqi oil sold under the first phase of the U.N. deal, designed to alleviate the impact of international sanctions on Iraq, has flowed via the Turkish pipeline to Ceyhan on the Mediterranean.
But some oil also has been lifted from Iraq's Gulf port Mina al-Bakr both for eastern markets and for the U.S. Gulf.
